analyst_view.overall: Palace are 18th with seven points and have lost three league games in a row without scoring, and one report says the board may decide Pierre Sage's future over the international break. Jean-Philippe Mateta is banned and Ismaila Sarr, Tomiyasu and Riad are out, so Nketiah and Strand Larsen are expected to lead the line. Andoni Iraola's Liverpool are winless in three after losing 3-2 at Fenerbahce, with Virgil van Dijk saying conceding three in each of those games is unsustainable; Gravenberch (heel) is the only doubt.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Palace have not scored in three league games and are without Mateta and Sarr, which points lower. But Liverpool have been leaking goals, including from set pieces at Fenerbahce, and Palace have the league's worst defence, so the two pull in opposite directions and we stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners, most of them Liverpool's. Without Mateta to hold the ball up, Palace are likely to sit deep and soak up pressure, which usually means more Liverpool corners, and Liverpool have won 51 in their last six games.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. A struggling home side and a Liverpool team needing a response could make it tense, but we found nothing on Tony Harrington or either team that clearly moves the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots. Liverpool should take plenty of shots against a deep Palace side, but Palace's own total looks likely to drop without Mateta and Sarr, so the two roughly cancel out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Palace have barely tested goalkeepers in their last three games and their two main attackers are missing, so we expect a slightly lower total even with Liverpool on top.
